title: Array Parameters
concept: Arrays are too large to pass whole, so only the 'first address' is sent to the function

steps.title: Including Header
steps.explanation:
`#include <stdio.h>` enables the output functions.

This lesson covers how arrays decay into addresses when passed as function arguments.

steps.title: printArr Function Definition
steps.explanation:
In `printArr(int arr[], int len)`, `arr[]` acts as a pointer in the function parameter.

That's why we must receive the length `len` separately to iterate safely.

steps.title: Starting the main Function
steps.explanation: The main frame is created and the array `data` is prepared.

steps.title: Array Declaration and Initialization
steps.explanation:
Array `data` stores 10, 20, 30 in contiguous memory.

The array name serves as a starting point representing the first element's address.

steps.title: Passing the Array (Array Decay)
steps.explanation:
When `printArr(data, 3);` is called, `data` decays to its starting address.

The function accesses the original location, not a copy of the array.

steps.title: Iterating with a for Loop
steps.explanation:
`arr[i]` prints the elements in order.

Internally, this is equivalent to pointer access `*(arr+i)`.

steps.title: Program Termination
steps.explanation:
`return 0;` ends the program.

Key point: when passing arrays as arguments, you must manage both the address and the length together.

quiz.question: When you declare void func(int a[100]), how does the compiler interpret it?
options: It interprets it as void func(int *a) (Pointer)
quiz.explanation:
The number inside the brackets is ignored.
An array declaration in a function parameter is always equivalent to a pointer declaration.

misconceptions.wrong: Arrays can be passed by Call by Value
misconceptions.why: If you really want to, you can wrap the array in a struct and pass the struct, which will create a copy (tip).

keyTakeaway: Array parameters are essentially pointers. That's why the original can be modified, and the length must be passed separately.
